asset_groups.path: src/spriteConstants.ts (7 SPRITE_ constants); src/tileValues.ts (about 198 export lines)
asset_groups.note: Sprite kinds and contiguous tile ID blocks. Data first.

inspiration: Water and woods are contiguous ID blocks with edge variants (src/tileValues.ts). A block-per-terrain-family scheme makes autotiling simple for our tile sets.
Seven sprite kinds cover moving city units, a roaming monster, a tornado and an explosion (src/spriteConstants.ts). A short list of sprite kinds keeps the cast small.
The monster appears in a separate TV-style window module (src/monsterTV.js). A side-screen event is a cheap news beat for the world.
Small 32 px sprites are numbered by group and frame (sprites/obj*.png). An easy naming scheme for an artist to follow.
A chunky display font is used for titles (css/style.css lines 22-25). Usable only under OFL conditions and not under the reserved name.

briefs.label: Side-window roaming monster
briefs.why: A monster seen through a separate small window makes the threat feel like news, and the main view stays clean.
briefs.keep: monster is a sprite kind of its own; shown in a side window rather than the main view; roams on its own timer
briefs.change: our own creature silhouette and proportions (a crawling bio-mech shape, not a lizard); a glowing eye band; a named faction badge in the window frame

briefs.label: Disaster and impact sprite pair
briefs.why: Separate sprite kinds for a disaster and for impact keep the effects readable and let each have its own timing.
briefs.keep: a moving disaster sprite and a separate impact sprite; each is its own kind; impact plays on contact
briefs.change: our own effect palette (ash, ember, cold blue instead of grey and orange); a different twist shape for the storm; a shockwave ring instead of a flat burst

briefs.label: Contiguous terrain ID blocks
briefs.why: Keeping each terrain family in one run of IDs, with edge variants in the same run, makes autotile rules short and clear.
briefs.keep: a run of IDs per terrain family; edge variants inside the family's run; a separate run for trees
briefs.change: our own number of edge variants and our own family order; a bridge family between water and land; labels on every ID from the start
briefs.ref: src/tileValues.ts (RIVER, REDGE, CHANNEL, LASTRIVEDGE, TREEBASE block near top of file)

briefs.label: Travelling unit sprite kinds
briefs.why: Moving city units as distinct sprite kinds let the player read traffic at a glance.
briefs.keep: a unit kind per mode of travel (rail, air, sea, road); units moving across the map on their own paths
briefs.change: our own vehicle designs in our fiction (hover-skiff, rail-glider, sky-barge); a mode that is a foot courier; a trail effect per unit

briefs.label: Numbered 32 px frame groups
briefs.why: Small, numbered frame groups keep sprite production simple for one artist and make animation frames easy to find.
briefs.keep: 32 px frames; numbered groups per object; frame index for animation
briefs.change: our own tile grid and frame counts; a palette ramp per group; a larger 48 px hero size for the player
